title: Module flatness over a local ring and its strict henselization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $K$ be a separable closure of $R/\mathfrak m$ (a separable algebraic extension which is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]), and let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be its strict henselization relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. For every $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $M$, give $M$ the $R$-action by restriction along the structural map $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Then $M$ is flat over $R$ if and only if $M$ is flat over $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, where module flatness means [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 05VL, lemma-flat-up-down-henselization, equivalence (1) and (3), applied to S=Spec R at its closed point. More on Algebra Tag 07QM supplies faithful flatness in its proof.

proof.text: Put $C=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Use the pointed etale algebra presentation of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. It is the triples presentation of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] at $\mathfrak m$: a pair $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ determines $\mathfrak q=\ker\chi$ and the field embedding $\phi:\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$ extending $S/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow K$, and a triple gives back $\chi$. The compatibility equations on morphisms agree by taking kernels and then fractions. These inverse identifications preserve the underlying $R$-algebra diagrams. Since $R$ is local, $R_{\mathfrak m}\cong R$ by $r/s\mapsto rs^{-1}$, so the triples theorem gives $C$ as their filtered colimit, with coprojections $\iota_t:S_t\to C$ and a map $\psi:C\to K$ whose kernel is the maximal ideal of $C$ and with $\psi\iota_t=\chi_t$.

source.place: Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different: triples, filteredness, and the first colimit; Tag 04GP, lemma-strict-henselization, local structure

proof.text: First suppose $M$ is flat over $C$. The structural map $R\to C$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] with $A=R$, $B=C$, and the given module $M$. This proves $R$-flatness for precisely the restricted action in the statement.

source.place: Tag 05VL, lemma-flat-up-down-henselization, (3) implies (1), using More on Algebra Tag 07QM and Algebra Tag 00HC

proof.text: Now suppose $M$ is flat over $R$. For a triple $t=(S_t,\mathfrak q_t,\phi_t)$ put $A_t=(S_t)_{\mathfrak q_t}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $s\notin\mathfrak q_t$, then $\psi(\iota_t(s))=\chi_t(s)\ne0$, so $\iota_t(s)$ is outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $C$ and is a unit. Thus $j_t:A_t\to C$, $a/s\mapsto\iota_t(a)\iota_t(s)^{-1}$, is a well-defined ring map extending $\iota_t$. Give $M$ its $A_t$-action through $j_t$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to $\operatorname{Spec}S_t\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak q_t$ over $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), its two local rings and germ maps are $(S_t)_{\mathfrak q_t}=A_t$ and $R_{\mathfrak m}=R$. The induced map is the localization of $R\to S_t$, hence its composite with $j_t$ is the structural map $R\to C$ (check $r/1$). Its restricted action on $M$ is therefore the stipulated $R$-action. The cited equivalence proves that $M$ is flat over every $A_t$.

source.place: Tag 05VL, proof of (1) implies (3), applying Tag 05BA, lemma-etale-flat-up-down-local-ring; Algebra Tag 04GW and Schemes Tag 01HV for localizations

proof.text: Let $\sum_{i=1}^n c_ix_i=0$ be any finite relation in the $C$-module $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], each coefficient $c_i$ comes from one pointed etale algebra $S_t$ in the colimit of step 1. Filteredness gives one object receiving all these finitely many objects; transport the representatives to it and still call it $t$, obtaining $b_i\in S_t$ with $\iota_t(b_i)=c_i$. For $n=0$ choose any object, which exists because the category is filtered. Put $a_i=b_i/1\in A_t$. The relation $\sum_i a_ix_i=0$ holds in $M$ with its $A_t$-action, because $j_t(a_i)=c_i$.

source.place: Tag 05UU, lemma-colimit-rings-flat (1), finite-coefficient argument expanded using Tag 00HK, lemma-flat-eq, and the representative property of filtered colimits

proof.text: Apply the forward direction of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion] to the $A_t$-flat module $M$ and the relation in step 4. It supplies $m\ge0$, $y_1,\ldots,y_m\in M$ and $d_{ij}\in A_t$ with $x_i=\sum_j d_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i a_id_{ij}=0$ for each $j$. Set $e_{ij}=j_t(d_{ij})\in C$. The definition of the restricted $A_t$-action gives $x_i=\sum_j e_{ij}y_j$. Applying $j_t$ to the coefficient equations gives $\sum_i c_ie_{ij}=0$. Thus the original arbitrary relation over $C$ is trivial. The reverse direction of the same equational criterion proves that $M$ is flat over $C$. Together with step 2 this proves the required equivalence.

Step 1: pairs (S,chi) and triples (S,q,phi) at m give isomorphic diagrams (q=ker chi, phi extends S/q into K to Frac(S/q), morphism conditions agree), so lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples gives filteredness, locality, psi and psi.iota_t=chi_t. Step 2: 07QM faithful flatness, then the faithful-flatness definition and Module.Flat.trans give flat over C => flat over R. Step 3: iota_t(s) is a unit for s outside q_t, so j_t:(S_t)_{q_t}->C is well defined; 05BA (lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness, no finiteness on M) together with affine-open-stalk-localization (c) gives M flat over every A_t, with the R-action checked. Steps 4-5: coefficients lift to one stage via the elementwise colimit lemma and filteredness (n=0 included); the 00HK equational criterion over A_t, pushed through j_t, makes every C-relation trivial, so M is flat over C. Not citing lem-weil-pbc-colimit-rings-flat (ring-map case only) or directed-union-subrings (j_t need not be injective) is correct. No duplicate of the item in the DAG (grep for 05VL, 05BA, 05UU and strict-henselization flatness), no cycle, no SGA. Small cases: R a field, R=Z_(p) with C/pC and Frac C, M=0.
